t: NoVideo: Pandas for the Post-Analog Video Age and the 40-Year Cycle
s: This article proposes a 'NoVideo' approach to content creation, advocating for manipulating video as abstract data using tools like Python's Pandas library, rather than traditional GUI editors. This method future-proofs skills against tech churn and aligns with generational cycles of knowledge evolution.
sub: Analog vs. Digital Video Editing Evolution (razor blades to magnetic tape to digital codecs like On2 VP6)
The 'Tech Churn' of Video Editing Software (Premiere, CapCut) and the 'Hard Pass' strategy
Leveraging Data Manipulation Skills (Pandas) for Video as Data (MoviePy, CLI, Jupyter Notebook)
Max Headroom's 'Blipverts' as a metaphor for abstract, signal-rich content
Generational Cycles, Durable Skills, and the 'All Signal, No Noise' philosophy
